result.rationale: The trajectory shows the rescue team consistently failing to make progress on the primary objective (rescue-two-civilians stays at 0/2 across all 6 turns) while suffering escalating health and spatial pressure. Engineer Imani is repeatedly attacked by Raider Holt (turns 1, 2, 3, 4) dropping from 100 to 17 health, and Medic Reyes took 21 damage on turn 1. The team's movement routes repeatedly funnel through junction-cover/storage-floor where Raider Holt holds position and attacks, while reactor-instability hazard drains health from anyone entering reactor zones (Security Chen and Hacker Nyx take 10 damage/turn). The rescue of civilian-sato was bound (turn 3) but Medic Reyes' extraction move to junction-cover was contested on turn 4 (target_zone_capacity_lost), blocking the escort route to rescue-airlock. The core bottleneck is that hostile pressure (Raider Holt's scatter-blast overwatch on the junction corridor, reactor hazard, zone capacity) blocks the actors from reaching/exploiting the rescue affordance before they can act on it. This is survival-spatial-pressure rather than an information problem (information is being gained steadily) or a local-policy-choice problem (the agents are attempting the correct rescue actions but being physically blocked/contested).
